# `unchecked-first-element`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a public function indexing a plain-slice parameter at zero without a
visible proof that the slice is non-empty.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

An empty plain slice has no first element, so indexing it traps in safe builds
and is undefined behavior when safety checks are disabled.

## When it fires

The rule checks externally callable boundaries with known plain slice types and
stays quiet for private invariants, fixed arrays, sentinel-terminated slices,
and visibly guarded accesses, including the unbraced branch of a length test
such as `if (needle.len == 1) return find(needle[0]);` and a short-circuit
guard such as `path.len >= 1 and (path[0] == '/' or path[0] == '\\')` or
`name.len < 2 or name[0] != 'u'`, with the length on either side of the
comparison. Uses inside `assert(...)` fail the same way the assertion would,
and functions whose doc comment says what they assert ("Asserts the value fits
within the provided `limbs_buffer`") document the precondition, so neither is
reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
pub fn first(bytes: []const u8) u8 {
    return bytes[0];
}
```
